sections.h2: Who keeps the property records in Sarasota County, FL?
sections.html:
The Sarasota County Clerk of the Circuit Court and Comptroller keeps the Official Records, which is where deeds, mortgages, liens, plats and court judgments about local land are filed. Anyone can search the index online, and a title company runs the same search before a Sarasota County sale closes.

The clerk's Official Records search opens to the public with no login. You can search by last or business name, by first name, by instrument number, by a filing date range, or by book and page. The index printed on the search screen starts on January 1, 1990.

A separate tab on the same screen covers marriage records, plats and condominiums, and property fraud alerts. Certified copies need a separate login, and the screen says approved requests may take up to 24 business hours to arrive in your mailbox.

sections.h2: What kinds of documents turn up in a Sarasota County records search?
sections.html:
The search covers more than a hundred document types, and several of them matter to a seller. The type menu includes deeds, mortgages, satisfactions of mortgage, claims of lien, releases of lien, lis pendens, final judgments, powers of attorney, easements, notices of commencement, tax liens and tax deeds.

When you search your own name or your property, look for these items before you list the house or accept an offer:

  • A mortgage with no matching satisfaction, which means the loan is still of record and must be paid at closing.
  • A claim of lien or notice to owner from a contractor, which can follow unpaid repair work.
  • A lis pendens, which signals a pending lawsuit that affects the property.
  • A judgment or tax lien filed under your name, which can attach to real estate you own.
  • An easement or restriction that a buyer's title search will pick up.

The type list also has probate-labeled entries such as letters of administration and personal representative oaths, so an inherited Sarasota County house usually leaves a visible paper trail.

sections.h2: What does the Sarasota County Clerk charge to record a document?
sections.html:
The clerk's fee page prints $10.00 for the first page of a standard document and $8.50 for each additional page. That applies to paper no larger than 8.5 by 14 inches. The clerk also lists plats at $30.00 for the first page and $15.00 for each added page.

Indexing is free for the first four names on a document, then $1.00 for each extra name. Florida's recording statute, s. 28.24(13), builds the per-page charge from a base fee plus a modernization trust fund charge and a technology charge, and the county figure above is what the clerk collects in total.

Sarasota County Clerk recording and related fees, as printed on the clerk's fee page

Notices of commencement and declarations of domicile also carry a $3.50 attestation fee. Ask the clerk's recording desk to confirm the total before you send a document in.

sections.h2: How much documentary stamp tax applies to a Sarasota County deed?
sections.html:
The clerk prints the deed rate as $0.70 per $100 of the consideration, which is the price paid for the property. Florida's deed statute, s. 201.02(1)(a), uses the same 70-cent rate, and the Department of Revenue says Miami-Dade is the only county with a different one.

The clerk's calculation tip is to round the consideration up to the next $100 before applying the rate, and the minimum tax is $0.70. A deed that conveys property is taxable whether or not it is recorded. The Department of Revenue states that every party to the document is liable regardless of who agrees to pay, so a sales contract usually decides who pays but the state can look to either side.

A new loan adds its own charges at recording. The clerk lists mortgage documentary stamps at $0.35 per $100 of the obligation and an intangible tax at $0.20 per $100, with the intangible tax computed on the exact loan amount and no rounding. These apply to the buyer's lender paperwork, not to your deed, but they appear on the same closing statement.

Some transfers are exempt. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed as not taxable, and deeds between spouses in a divorce for the marital home are exempt under s. 201.02(7). Qualifying exemptions must be evident on the face of the document, so ask the closing agent to confirm the wording before you sign.

sections.h2: How do you spot and stop deed fraud in Sarasota County?
sections.html:
Sign up for the clerk's free Property Fraud Alerts. The service emails you whenever a deed, mortgage or similar instrument is recorded in Sarasota County under the name you registered, which gives you a chance to react to a forged filing quickly.

The Sarasota County Property Appraiser has also encouraged owners to register, and the clerk's search screen has a Property Fraud Alerts tab. Register the owner's name and any business name used to hold title, and do it before a house sits empty or changes hands.

If an alert shows a recording you did not authorize, contact the clerk's office and an attorney promptly, and keep the instrument number from the alert. You can also register a business name if the house sits in an LLC.

sections.h2: How do records and property tax connect when you sell in Sarasota County?
sections.html:
The recorded deed is what tells the property appraiser and tax collector that ownership changed, so a late recording can delay bills reaching the new owner. The Sarasota County Tax Collector says a delay in recording a deed can leave an owner without a timely bill.

Taxes are usually prorated on the closing statement. The tax collector's page says the seller gives the buyer credit for the part of the year the seller owned the house, and no money goes to the tax collector as a partial payment. The buyer is responsible for the whole bill. Our Sarasota County property tax guide covers the calendar and discounts.

A sale also ends the Save Our Homes cap. Florida's Department of Revenue says a change of ownership resets the property to just value the next January 1, with exceptions such as transfers between spouses.

sections.h2: What should you check before recording or selling a Sarasota County house?
sections.html:
Pull the current owner's recording history and compare it to what the buyer's title agent will find. A short pre-listing checklist saves time:

  • Search your name and the parcel for open mortgages, liens and judgments.
  • Confirm every owner on the deed is alive, competent and able to sign.
  • Ask your closing agent which exemptions, if any, apply to the deed stamps.
  • Have the deed signed in front of two witnesses; Florida's s. 689.01 requires two subscribing witnesses for a conveyance of land.
  • Register for fraud alerts before the house is listed or left vacant.

If you are selling an inherited property, the clerk's record will show whether letters of administration were issued, and summary administration is available under s. 735.201 for a non-exempt estate not above $150,000 or a decedent dead more than two years.

faqs.q: How do I search Sarasota County Official Records for free?
faqs.a: Use the clerk's online Official Records search, which needs no login. Enter a last name, business name, instrument number or a date range. The index shown on the screen begins January 1, 1990.

faqs.q: How much does recording a deed cost in Sarasota County?
faqs.a: The clerk charges $10.00 for the first page and $8.50 for each additional page of a standard document. Indexing is free for four names and $1.00 per extra name. Deed documentary stamp tax is separate, at $0.70 per $100 of consideration.

faqs.q: Who pays deed stamps when a Sarasota County house sells?
faqs.a: Florida law makes every party to the document liable, whoever the contract says will pay. In practice the purchase contract assigns the cost, and the closing agent collects it at recording.

faqs.q: Can I get a certified copy of a recorded document?
faqs.a: Yes. The clerk offers certification at $2.00 per document and a certified copy login on the Official Records screen. Approved requests can take up to 24 business hours to appear in your mailbox.

faqs.q: Does selling to a cash buyer change the recording steps?
faqs.a: No. A cash sale still ends with a deed recorded in the Official Records and the same documentary stamp tax. A title company still searches for liens and mortgages before closing.
